packageRules.description: Keep the ranges, move the floor. 'replace' only rewrites a range when the new version falls outside it, so an in-range release (next 16.3.0 inside ^16.0.7) produced no diff and no PR. This also overrides the :pinDevDependencies that config:best-practices pulls in — packageRules beat top-level config, so it has to live here.
Peers and engines keep their ranges — a peer range is a compatibility statement, not an install instruction
All dev tooling lands in one PR
React and Next move in lockstep, types included. Declared after the devDependencies rule so it wins for @types/react.
CI actions in one PR — grouping keeps the digest refresh in the same branch as the version bump instead of opening a second PR next to it
